short: Headphone-integrated textile EMG (M05) is standard, after a dry-electrode necklace; 96% on ten words is one random sample split over four people, speaker separation not stated.
position: The paper [@tang2025] changes the sensor (M05): four dry textile EMG electrodes in a headphone earmuff. This is standard: moving dry electrodes from the face into a worn object follows a dry-electrode necklace [@wu2024necklace], and no condition compares the earmuff with conventional electrodes on the same words. The decoder (M06), a 1D SE-ResNet, is standard; its claimed adaptation to contact quality rests on one example (Fig. 5). The 96% on ten words comes from one random 80/20 sample split pooled over four people, without seeds, repeated runs or stated speaker separation (Sec. III.A), and rests on about 200 test samples (inference from Fig. 4). "Real-time" and "low-power" are not measured.
